items.title: Lou Donaldson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: he knew Lester Young’s “Just You, Just Me,” ... If you cut it down, he sounded like Lester Young

ctx.x: When you got to Greensboro, did jazz start to enter the picture more?

No, not really. Because see, back then you couldn’t play jazz in college. If they caught you practicing jazz in the practice room, you couldn’t practice any more. They didn’t like jazz. They didn’t like nothing but classical and band music—the teachers. But what happened to me, a guy came from Seattle, Washington, named Billy Tolles, and he had been around all the musicians, and he had his saxophone. He could play. Excellent player. He knew Coleman Hawkins’ “Body and Soul” and he knew Lester Young’s “Just You,…
him $2 or $3 to bring us back some jazz records, and he would do it.
